statements.says: Every commit a Session makes carries a Skillworks-Session trailer holding the session.id that telemetry carries, so a commit leads to the Session that wrote it.
A PreToolUse hook in the Plugin adds the trailer to each git commit Claude runs.
The hook denies, with its reason, a commit it cannot rewrite safely, so Claude runs it again in a plain form.
The driver picks each Session's id before it starts the Session and records it beside the ticket's worktree.
The Keep names every Session that ran on the ticket.
The trailer is optional where a ticket Lands.
An amend by a second Session adds a second trailer line, and both stay.
A link that goes missing without a word is worse than none, because a reader trusts the history that has it.
The Keep makes its commit inside a script, where no hook sees it.
The Keep names every Session because the Session running at the stop never reported its id.
The trailer is optional where a ticket Lands because the hook and the Keep are what make it reliable.
Both trailer lines stay after an amend because both Sessions wrote the commit.

A git prepare-commit-msg hook was rejected, because git takes its hooks from each clone and never from a plugin, so a fresh clone with nothing installed would make commits with no trailer and no warning.
Reusing the Claude-Session key was rejected, because Claude Code on the web writes it with a URL, so one key would hold two kinds of value.
Letting a commit the hook cannot rewrite run as it is was rejected, because it is the quiet miss the trailer exists to prevent.
